A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 13-page IDProtector paper, including references and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the scientific content is unchanged; differences are confined to first-page author and version metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original identity-protection experiments on CelebA and VGG Face, runtime and robustness measurements, and appendix analyses of prior channels and target embeddings.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 3–7 and the appendix training curves and generated-image examples.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same ViT noise encoder, prior channels, embedding-attack objectives, regularization losses, affine augmentation, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CelebA training data and CelebA/VGG Face evaluation coverage. The unseen-generator evaluations and image-distortion scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains ACE, AdvDM, Anti-DreamBooth, PhotoGuard, SimAC, the unprotected reference, and the proposed PGD variant. Table 6 retains the same Adaptive PGD comparison; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Both retain 190,000 training images, 50 test images from each dataset, five prompts per dataset, and the 9/255 perturbation budget. Metrics, preprocessing, training settings, and distortion procedures are identical.

E4.justification: The distortion robustness tests in Section 5.4/Table 6, prior-channel convergence analysis in Appendix A/Figure 9, and alternative-target-embedding ablation in Appendix B/Table 7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including Table 3's averaging over five prompts and the appendix training-curve displays. No run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance analyses are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged, including the appendix results. For example, Table 3 reports the same CelebA/InstantID ISM of 0.231 for IDProtector, and Table 4 retains its 0.173-second runtime.

T1.justification: The problem definition, optimization objectives, and affine-transform and prior-construction mathematics in Equations 1–8 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about feed-forward identity protection, efficiency, universality, robustness, imperceptibility, and generalization to unseen and closed-source generators.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the PGD tradeoff, generalization results, and shortcomings of SER-FIQ remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation that perturbations are not fully invisible and require an effectiveness–imperceptibility tradeoff.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same ViT-S/8 architecture, Table 2 hyperparameters, batch size of 112, four 80GB H100 GPUs, ten-day training duration, and appendix prior-construction details. The project link and its embedded destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 32 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to tuning-based customization defenses and the claimed gap in protection against encoder-based generation remain identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds a corresponding-author marker to Hai Ci and updates the arXiv stamp from v1 dated 16 December 2024 to v2 dated 4 February 2025. Body wording, section organization, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10, Tables 1–7, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–13 are pixel-identical; the first-page differences are limited to author and version text.

improvement.justification: The only edits are the corresponding-author designation and version/date stamp. Scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations remain identical, including the appendices, so there is no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
